title: Termwise direct sums of complexes of modules are direct sums in D(A)
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, let $D(A)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $A$-modules, and let $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed family of cochain complexes of $A$-modules. Then the termwise direct sum $\bigoplus_{i\in I}K_i^\bullet$, together with the images in $D(A)$ of the coprojections $K_i^\bullet\to\bigoplus_{i\in I}K_i^\bullet$, is a direct sum (coproduct) of the $K_i^\bullet$ in $D(A)$.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 07D9 (lemma-derived-products), clauses (1)-(2), applied to the Grothendieck abelian category of A-modules

proof.text: For each degree r, define the termwise direct sum by $(\bigoplus_i K_i)^r=\bigoplus_i K_i^r$ and take the direct sum of the differentials. The differential squares to zero and the canonical inclusions are chain maps, by the cochain-complex definition.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 07D9 (lemma-derived-products), construction of the direct-sum complex

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian], the category of $A$-modules is Grothendieck abelian, so filtered colimits of $A$-modules are exact. A set-indexed direct sum $\bigoplus_{i\in I}$ is the filtered colimit over finite subsets $J\subseteq I$ of the finite direct sums $\bigoplus_{i\in J}$, which are exact in any abelian category; hence set-indexed direct sums of $A$-modules are exact. Therefore kernels, images and cohomology of the termwise differential commute with the direct sum, $H^r(\bigoplus_iK_i^\bullet)\cong\bigoplus_iH^r(K_i^\bullet)$, and a family of quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] has a quasi-isomorphic termwise direct sum.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 07D9 (lemma-derived-products), clauses (1)-(2), exactness of direct sums in A-Mod

proof.text: Let $X$ be an object of $D(A)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence] ($\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]) there is a quasi-isomorphism $X\to I^\bullet$ with $I^\bullet$ K-injective, i.e. $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(N,I^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic $N$; taking $H^0$, every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I^\bullet$ is null-homotopic, which is the K-injectivity hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. So $X\cong QI^\bullet$ in $D(A)$ and it suffices to treat $X=QI^\bullet$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], applied to $\bigoplus_iK_i^\bullet$ and to each $K_i^\bullet$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(\bigoplus_iK_i^\bullet,I^\bullet)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(\bigoplus_iK_i^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(K_i^\bullet,I^\bullet)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(K_i^\bullet,I^\bullet)$, compatibly with composition with the coprojections. The middle identification $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(\bigoplus_iK_i^\bullet,I^\bullet)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(K_i^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ is the degreewise coproduct universal property for chain maps and for homotopies (a homotopy out of the direct sum is a family of homotopies). Hence the images of the coprojections satisfy the coproduct universal property in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 07D9 (lemma-derived-products), clauses (1)-(2), coproduct universal property
